subject: bengal tiger
title: One Tiger Killed 436 People. Its Broken Teeth Explained Why

scenes.text: One tiger. 436 people. And two broken teeth explain it.
Nepal, around 1900. A Bengal tigress starts taking villagers. Hunters fail. The army is sent in, and drives her across the river into India.
In the hills of Kumaon she keeps going, covering up to 32 kilometers a day between villages. Guinness lists her as the deadliest animal on record.
In 1907 the hunter Jim Corbett follows the trail from her last victim, a 16-year-old girl, near Champawat. Three hundred villagers form a line. She is shot.
Then the examination. The upper and lower canine teeth on her right side were broken, from an old gunshot wound.
She could no longer catch deer. So she switched to the one prey that couldn't outrun her.

description:
A single tigress is credited with an estimated 436 human deaths in Nepal and India, and a post-mortem found a reason.
The Champawat tiger began attacking villagers in western Nepal in the late 1800s; after hunters failed, the Nepalese army drove her across the Sarda river into the Kumaon hills of India, where the killing continued. Guinness World Records lists her as the tiger with the most human fatalities. Jim Corbett shot her in 1907 near Champawat. Her upper and lower right canines were broken from an old gunshot wound, which Corbett believed stopped her from hunting her natural prey.
Do you think the hunter who shot her was right to blame the injury?
first_comment: Corbett later became a conservationist, and India's first national park is named after him. Which famous animal story should we tell next?
